expressions.E1_dot: s = sum_{i=0..7} q_i*k_i, 8-dim dot product (attention-score style), mixed-sign O(0.1..0.9) inputs fixed below
expressions.E2_gate: h = tanh(sum_{i=0..3} q_i*k_i) * v, tanh gate times value (GLU-style), 4-dim
expressions.E3_norm: out = (sum_{i=0..7} x_i*x_i)^(-1) * x_0, RMS-style normalization via exact integer-power reciprocal

claims.text: Drift is bounded and small: for every node of E1/E2/E3 (inputs excluded from the comparison floor), the float-vs-exact relative error of BOTH the forward value and the gradient is < 1e-13; the subset graphs E1 and E2 additionally satisfy < 1e-14.
claims.derivation: a-priori rounding bound: each float op contributes <= U = 2^-52 ~ 2.23e-16 relative; graphs have <= 17 internal ops with amplification <= ~10 (mixed-sign sum ratio |sum|/sum|terms| ~ 1.5 for E1, ~1 for E2/E3); worst case ~ 17*U*10 ~ 3.8e-14, so 1e-13 carries honest margin; measured maxima are reported and expected tighter
claims.verdict_rule: PASS iff all rel errs < 1e-13 AND max(E1,E2 rel errs) < 1e-14; else FAIL with the offending node receipted

claims.text: Exactness is real and consistent: (a) engine exact-mode backward (Value.grad_twin) and auditor.exact_grads over the float tape rows agree EXACTLY (Fraction equality, zero tolerance) on every audited node of E1/E2/E3; (b) every exact gradient denominator has <= 1000 decimal digits; (c) at least one exact rational gradient is receipted verbatim (numerator, denominator, digit counts) in gradients.json.
claims.derivation: both exact paths do Fraction arithmetic on the same frozen-float graph; dyadic inputs keep denominators small (~16-34 digits); reciprocal breaks dyadicity but numerator(y)~11 digits for E3; lcm-chain worst case ~ hundreds of digits, so 1000 is a 10x-margin honest bound
claims.verdict_rule: PASS iff exact equality holds everywhere AND max denominator digits <= 1000 AND gradients.json non-empty; else FAIL

claims.text: Negative control: corrupting ONE node's float gradient by exactly 1 ulp (nextafter AWAY from the exact value) is FLAGGED by the stochastic auditor (audit(rows, corrupted_grads, mode='stochastic', seed=0)) for EVERY auditable node across E1/E2/E3; flagged means some reported path (s, a=target) has rel_corrupted - rel_clean >= 2e-17 where rel_clean is the same-seed audit of the uncorrupted grads.
claims.derivation: STRUCTURAL prediction, registered before measurement: the auditor always promotes every sink and walks ALL ancestors of each sampled node; every node feeds some sink, so the union of audited paths covers every node's gradient regardless of the Bernoulli(1/sqrt(N)) draw - detection is structural, not stochastic. Honest corollary receipted either way: the 1/sqrt(N) economy governs path MULTIPLICITY (and reporting), not coverage, because exact_grads is computed unconditionally. If ANY node's injection goes undetected, that is an honest FAIL and is reported as such.
claims.verdict_rule: PASS iff 100% of injected nodes flagged; any miss reported as FAIL with the node id, seed, and clean/corrupted rel values

claims.text: Determinism receipts: for each of E1/E2/E3 the hash-chained tape verifies (Tape.verify() == (True, None)) after a taped float backward, and tape.replay(rows, root=sink) reproduces the live float gradients BITWISE (exact float equality per node).
claims.derivation: micrograd-quilt design law 2 (tape as determinism/regression guard); replay applies EFFECT rows in the same accumulation order as live backward
claims.verdict_rule: PASS iff all three graphs verify AND replay == live bitwise; else FAIL with the mismatching node receipted
